name: Working for Nature / Mahi mō te Taiao grant
summary: Contestable council grants for community groups, businesses, landowners and individuals in Marlborough to restore native habitat and control pests, plus a small environmental advocacy category. Paid by reimbursement against project milestones.

amount.note: Cap for the pest-control category; habitat restoration is capped lower and advocacy lower again

calls.label: April application month
calls.recurring: Applications open 1 to 30 April; outcomes notified by July

status.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April.

recurring.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their grant by July.

applicant_types.quote: One application per category is permitted annually from community organisations, businesses, landowners (including farming, forestry, winegrowing) and individuals.

geography.quote: Marlborough has been identified as one of five centres of biodiversity in New Zealand due to the concentration of endemic species

access.quote: The contestable grant scheme is administered by a sub-committee of the Environment Committee, and operates using a reimbursement model.

window.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April.

amount.quote: Protecting Marlborough: These projects control animal and plant pests that are threatening native wildlife and habitats. Grants are up to $15,000 per applicant in any one year.
